Azalea: A small-flower print named for the week in April every golfer circles on the calendar. It works the other fifty-one weeks too.
Gold Dust: White with gold flecked all through it and a gold collar. Wear it with the Carver and go full matching set. We won't judge.
Shadow: Charcoal on black, mottled like the light under trees. Dark enough for dinner after, with enough going on that it's not just a black polo.
Signature Black: No print, just black, with the clover and the wordmark in gold on the chest. For when your swing is loud enough already.
Contour: Contour lines across white, like a map of the green you're about to misread. Tonal, so it only shows up close.
Marble: Gold and teal veining across white, like a cracked marble slab. The loudest shirt in the rack, and it knows it.
Gold Carnation: White carnations on gold, with a gold collar. There's no version of this one that blends in.
Frost: A frosted gray break across white. Pattern without color, for the days you'd rather keep it cool.
Cruiser: Rows of little carts on sage green. Someone's going to ask what's on your shirt, and you're going to enjoy answering.
Nightshade: White line flowers on black, with a white collar and placket. Looks like you've got your life together, even if your short game doesn't.
Swirl: A tonal swirl through white with a blade collar, so there's nothing at your throat. Goes with everything in your bag.
Spot: Off-white with a faint speckle and a blade collar. The quietest one we make.
Blackout: Black on black, mottled, with a blade collar. Lucky in the bag, nothing shouting on the shirt.
